newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells magnetic heads maker to U.S. firm.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells magnetic heads maker to U.S. firm.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Friday it had sold 80 percent of the Magnetic Heads plant to U.S. firm DRS Ahead Technology for $340,000 after deals with another U.S. buyer twice fell through.
The remaining 20 percent of the capital will be offered at preferential prices to the company's employees.

The new owner, Silicon Valley-based DRS Ahead Technology, has agreed to invest $2.3 million in the company over the next five years, to preserve the existing 92 job positions and to increase them to 139 by the end of the period.
Magnetic Heads, based in Bulgaria's southwest town of Razlog, produces magnetic heads for tape drives, hard disk drives, card readers and writers and magnetic sensors.
Its 1996 turnover amounted to 6.2 billion levs with 95 percent of it production exported, mainly to West European countries and the United States.
Debt-ridden Bulgaria currently badly needs income from privatisation to meet huge foreign debt payments.
Previous sell-off deals with U.S. buyer Design Review International fell through in 1993 and 1994. -- Galina Sabeva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
